summary: Describes route reflection, a method to reduce the need for a full mesh of internal BGP sessions inside a network. It was experimental and was replaced by RFC 4456.

eli5.summary: Instead of every person calling every other person, everyone calls one helper who passes the news along to the others.

questions: how to avoid full mesh ibgp
how does route reflection reduce ibgp sessions
what are originator id and cluster list
subtitle: A technique to reduce the complexity of internal BGP network topology.

tldr.problem: Inside an autonomous system, all BGP routers must be fully meshed, which requires maintaining n*(n-1)/2 connections. This becomes unscalable as networks grow.
tldr.mechanism: A route reflector router can reflect internal BGP routes learned from other routers to each other, eliminating the need for a full mesh among client routers.
tldr.outcome: Networks can be organized into clusters with a single route reflector per cluster, reducing configuration complexity and IBGP session count. This was experimental and was later standardized as RFC 4456.

today: RFC 1966 is experimental and was obsoleted by RFC 4456, which standardized route reflection as a recommended technique for scaling internal BGP networks. Route reflection is widely deployed in modern networks.

sections.title: The Full Mesh Problem
sections.content:
When multiple BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) routers operate inside a single network, the protocol requires every internal router to exchange routing information with every other internal router. For n routers, this demands n times (n minus 1) divided by 2 unique connections.

A network with just 10 internal BGP routers needs 45 such connections. With 100 routers, it jumps to 4,950. This full mesh becomes a scaling problem: bandwidth usage grows quadratically, router CPU burden increases, and configuration becomes unwieldy.
sections.eli5: If every kid in a class has to tell every other kid their favorite color, and there are 30 kids, that's a lot of talking. It's much easier to have one kid listen and then announce it to everyone else.

sections.title: Route Reflection
sections.content:
Route Reflection relaxes the requirement that all internal BGP speakers must be fully meshed. A designated route reflector listens to external routing information and internal announcements, then selectively re-advertises (or reflects) them to other internal routers. This breaks the strict peering rule that internal peers do not re-advertise to other internal peers.

The route reflector router acts as an intermediary, allowing client routers to avoid direct peering with each other. A route reflector along with its client routers form a cluster. Client routers within a cluster need not be fully meshed; they only peer with their route reflector.
sections.eli5: A special helper router listens to routing announcements from other routers and passes them along to the right neighbors, like a post office sorting mail.

sections.title: Architecture and Operation
sections.content:
A route reflector categorizes its internal peers into two groups: client peers and non-client peers. When the route reflector receives a route, it applies reflection rules. Routes from a non-client peer go to all client peers. Routes from a client peer go to all non-client peers and to other client peers (except the originator). Routes from external BGP peers go to both groups.

A network may have many route reflectors. Multiple route reflectors can be configured to form a backbone where they are all non-clients of each other (fully meshed among themselves) while managing clusters of client routers. This design allows gradual migration: old BGP speakers that do not understand route reflection can coexist as either client or non-client routers.
sections.eli5: The helper has two types of helpers to manage: regular helpers who talk to each other, and special student helpers who only talk to the main helper.

sections.title: Preventing Routing Loops
sections.content:
When routes are reflected, they can loop back to routers that already know them, especially if misconfiguration occurs. Route Reflection defines two new optional BGP attributes to detect and prevent loops.

The ORIGINATOR_ID attribute (type code 9) carries the router ID of the router that originated a route in the local network. A route reflector must never send a route back to the router specified in the ORIGINATOR_ID. The CLUSTER_LIST attribute (type code 10) is a sequence of cluster IDs representing the reflection path a route has taken. If a route reflector sees its own cluster ID in the CLUSTER_LIST, it knows the route has already passed through its cluster and discards it.
sections.eli5: The mail gets a stamp each time a helper passes it along. If the helper sees their own stamp, they know the mail already came through them and they throw it away to prevent it going in circles.

sections.title: Redundant Route Reflectors
sections.content:
A single route reflector per cluster creates a single point of failure. To provide redundancy, multiple route reflectors can serve the same cluster. When multiple route reflectors exist in a cluster, they must all be configured with a common CLUSTER_ID (a 4-byte value) so that each route reflector can identify routes coming from other reflectors in the same cluster and avoid excessive reflection.

A cluster without a configured CLUSTER_ID uses the router ID of the route reflector as its identifier. With multiple reflectors and a shared CLUSTER_ID, both reflectors can reflect routes without creating loops, and if one reflector fails, the cluster continues to work.
sections.eli5: Instead of one helper, you can have two helpers with the same name tag, so if one is sick the other one can take over.
